message.content:
You are joining a reverse-engineering project. First read /tmp/notes/ARCH.md completely — it explains the task, the strict rules (black-box only: never decompile/trace/read the original binary, never use `executable serve`, never run fmt in place on repo files; no internet), the repo layout/status, and the comparison tools in /tmp/agent-tools/.

Your job: core features that cut across all diagram families — byte-identical to the original:
1. Paint: `gradient(--a, --b[, --c…])` (auto angle), `linear-gradient(angle, …)`, `radial-gradient(…)`, gradients on stroke, oklch()/rgb()/hsl() stops — `<linearGradient>`/`<radialGradient>` defs with hashed ids (find the hashed string; util::hash8 = FNV-1a64 folded), `fill="url(#…)"` usage in rules/inline styles, and how vars inside gradients register. Tests: test_doc_examples spec_21 (+blocks/spec_021), test_samples paint.lini, hero.lini, pcb.lini (the root `fill: gradient(...)` canvas). Root canvas `fill:` with gradients too.
2. Generic validation with the original's exact messages/codes/spans and ORDER of checks: unknown property (with "did you mean" + the JSON "suggestion" object: `{"span":{…},"replacement":"color","applicability":"machine-applicable"}` inside the diagnostic — check diag.rs JSON output against `executable --json`), "'X' has no meaning on '|Y|'", scene-config-only properties (`'density' is scene config`…), value-shape errors (`'width' takes a number — a '%' is a colour component`, `expected 1, 2, or 4 values, got 3`, `'font-weight' takes …`, `'fit' must be …`), unknown function/name in expressions (`unknown function 'wave'` — note expressions in `points:` are evaluated lazily: spec_29 errors at the use site 2:10), `'|line|' requires 'points'` (exists in chart.rs validate — keep consistent), layout-membership errors that aren't family-specific. Build a corpus of hundreds of erroneous/odd snippets and compare first-error output (text and `--json`). Family-specific errors (sequence/tree/schematic/drawing/chart membership) belong to other agents working in parallel — don't duplicate those.
3. CLI rendering modes: `--static` (inline every `var()` as its literal light value — or the chosen theme's — and outline all text to glyph paths: `<path id="lini-g{size*100?}{weight}-{gid}" d="…"/>` defs built from the bundled TTF outlines (src/font.rs has glyph outlines; quadratic → `Q` with implied on-curve midpoints, numbers trimmed), `<use href transform="translate(x y) scale(s -s)">`, the `.lini-canvas` background rect, the shorter stylesheet; verify on many asset files), `--embed-font` (base64 `@font-face` for each used family×weight — "Lini Sans"/"Lini Sans Code" — font bytes are in fonts/*.ttf; check order and where they go), `--theme FILE` (a CSS file of `--lini-*` overrides; error text when unreadable is known: see main.rs), `--theme A/B` pairs (theme.rs), `--no-fs`, `--format html` (exists), `-o FILE`, shadows under themes (flood-color should follow the theme — currently hardcoded light).
Hook these into render.rs/main.rs with care (other agents edit render.rs in parallel; keep your changes as contained as possible, e.g. a post-processing or a dedicated module src/static.rs, src/gradient.rs, src/validate.rs).

Before committing, run the full asset comparison in several modes: default, `-a --static`, `-a --embed-font`, `-a "--theme dark"`, `-a "--theme high-contrast"`, `-a "--theme light/dark"`, `-a --json` (`python3 /tmp/agent-tools/cmpw.py /tmp/bin-core/executable -a "…" /workspace/assets/test_doc_examples/*.lini /workspace/assets/test_samples/*.lini /workspace/assets/test_doc_examples/blocks/*.lini`; default start: 171/246) and make sure nothing regresses; keep `-a desugar`, `-a "fmt --stdout"`, `-a highlight` at 246/246. Commit on your branch and report pass counts per mode, features, shared-file edits and gaps.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.

# Lini reimplementation — notes for contributors

## The task (read carefully)
We are reimplementing, from scratch in Rust (std only, no crates), a closed binary at
`/workspace/executable` ("lini 1.1.0", a diagram compiler: Lini source → SVG). Our build must
produce byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit codes for every input. Hidden tests compare outputs
exactly, so a test only passes when the whole output matches.

RULES (strict):
- Learn behaviour ONLY by running `/workspace/executable` with inputs and reading its output.
  NEVER decompile/disassemble it, never use strace/ltrace/gdb on it, never read its bytes.
- No internet, no looking for lini source code anywhere. std-only Rust.
- Do not run `./compile.sh` in /workspace (it would try to overwrite the original binary).
- Keep scratch scripts OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/<you>/). Non-Rust code in the repo is limited.

- NEVER run `executable fmt FILE` (without --stdout) or our fmt on files inside /workspace —
  fmt rewrites files in place. Copy inputs to /tmp/<you>/ first if you need in-place commands.
- Do NOT use `executable serve` or anything it serves over HTTP. Stick to the CLI
  (compile, --json, --static, --embed-font, desugar, fmt, highlight, theme) as your oracle.

## Docs / samples
- `/workspace/README.md` (overview), `/workspace/assets/` — sample inputs:
  `test_doc_examples/*.lini` (one per documented property, plus SPEC/SKILL snippets),
  `test_samples/*.lini` (larger feature boards), `test_images/mark.png`.
  The hidden test-suite is very likely more files of the same kinds.

## Build & compare
- In your checkout: `cargo build --release` → `target/release/lini`.
- Copy it to a private dir under the name `executable` (help/usage text uses argv[0]):
  `mkdir -p /tmp/bin-<you> && cp target/release/lini /tmp/bin-<you>/executable`
- Tools in `/tmp/agent-tools/` (shared, read-only use):
  - `cmpw.py /tmp/bin-<you>/executable [-a "args"] files...` → OK n / m and failing files.
  - `dw /tmp/bin-<you>/executable file.lini [args]` → diff (original vs ours).
  - `rr 'lini source' [args]` → run the ORIGINAL on a snippet (prints output + [exit N]).
  - `rm2 /tmp/bin-<you>/executable 'lini source' [args]` → diff on a snippet.
- Font metric helper (python, for exploration): `/tmp/scripts/tw.py` / `/tmp/scripts/ttf.py`.

## Code map (src/)
- `main.rs` — CLI dispatch (`cli.rs` emulates clap), `compile_src()` pipeline:
  parse → `scene::build_sheet` → `scene::Builder` (node tree) → `compile::compute` (cascade +
  `Computed` per node) → `layout::measure(ctx, 0, None)` → `render::render`.
- `lexer.rs`, `parser.rs`, `ast.rs` — tokens / recursive descent / syntax tree. Errors are
  fail-fast: first `Diag` aborts (`diag.rs` has codes & text/JSON rendering).
- `scene.rs` — `SheetModel` (root config decls, vars, bindings, type rules, defines, classes,
  id rules, link rules), `Node` (prim, `chain` = type chain most-derived first, id, classes,
  inline decls, text, children, `props` = cascaded decls map, layout fields w/h = rect size,
  x/y = centre relative to parent centre), `Builder` (statements → nodes).
- `types.rs` — built-in type registry (name, primitive, base, defaults as lini decl text).
- `style.rs` — value helpers (`value_num(s)`, `ident_of`, colour/weight/dash serialisation).
- `compile.rs` — `Ctx` (all state), `cascade()` (type chain base-first: defaults then user
  `|type|` rules; then classes; id rules; inline), `compute()` fills `ctx.comp[i]: Computed`
  (font size/weight/family, padding, gap, direction, align, justify, width/height, stroke…).
- `layout.rs` — `measure()` dispatch (text, line/poly/path geometry, chart hook, grid, flow).
  `outer(ctx,i)` = rect size + stroke width when stroke != none (text: its box).
- `render.rs` — SVG + stylesheet. CSS rules are collected as (slot, text) and sorted by
  `SLOT_ORDER`; families push extra rules into `out.extra_rules`. Root `--lini-*` vars are
  emitted for every var referenced (`use_var(&mut out.vars, name)`), sorted by name.
  The scope class is `lini-scope-` + hash8(style text written with `.lini` as scope).
- `util.rs` — `f4()` (all coordinates: `{:.4}` then trim zeros; "-0"→"0"), `hash8()` (FNV-1a 64,
  folded hi^lo, 8 hex), `xml_escape`, `base64`, `levenshtein`.
- `font.rs` — bundled TTFs (extracted via `--embed-font`); `text_width(family, weight, size, s)`.
- `markers.rs` — arrow/dot/diamond line-end markers. `geom.rs` — SVG path bbox.

## Facts learned so far (all verified against the original)
- Text box: width = Σ advances·size/1000 (+ letter-spacing·(n−1)); height = size for one line,
  n·1.2·size + (n−1)·line-spacing for n lines. Text renders `<text class="lini-text" x y
  dy="0.358em">`; multi-line uses tspans (first y = centre − (n−1)·pitch/2 + 0.358·size).
- Inline `style="…"` on a node = its own/inline decls minus those equal to what its CSS rules
  (type chain + classes) already give, in CSS_ORDER.
- Indentation: 2 spaces per nesting level; scene children start at 4.
- Only the first error is reported (`file:line:col: error: msg`, exit 1); warnings are printed
  before the SVG and do not change exit code (unless --strict).

## Status (after wave 2) — modules now in the tree
- `chart.rs` + `chart/*` (charts & pies, done), `table.rs` (tables/entity), `page.rs` (sheets,
  title-blocks), `sketch.rs` (draw: pen) + `drawing.rs` (stack/drawing layouts, holes, patterns,
  revolve/break/thread, planes, magnifier; see its notes on tagged segments, `drawing::ps`,
  `pattern_copy`), `icon.rs`/`image.rs` + `data/icons.txt`, `links.rs` + `route.rs` + `wires.rs`
  (link rendering + orthogonal router; `ctx.link_geo`), `desugar.rs` + `desugar/*` (complete; it
  contains its own lowering for tables, pages, trees/mindmaps, drawings, schematics incl. wire
  routing in `desugar/schematic.rs`/`sch_geo.rs` — reuse ideas from there), `format*` (fmt, done),
  `highlight.rs` (done).
- Pipeline (main.rs `compile_src`): parse → build_sheet → Builder (build_stmts, icon::validate,
  resolve_links, page::root_fixup, unworn_class_warnings) → Ctx → compute → drawing::expand
  (+recompute) → chart::validate → page::scale_units → drawing::prepare → image::check_sizes →
  layout::measure → drawing::size_warnings → links::compute → render → table::check_grids.
- Current asset pass rate: 146/209 (+25/37 in test_doc_examples/blocks). desugar/fmt/highlight
  are 246/246 on the corpus.

## Links (already in place)
- `scene::Builder::resolve_links()` resolves every link statement after the node tree is built:
  ids are scoped (a node with an id opens a scope for its descendants; anonymous containers are
  transparent), bare unknown names auto-create `|box#name| "name"` appended to the container,
  dotted paths resolve scope by scope, chains/fans expand in statement order (cartesian, `from`
  outer). Result: `ctx.links: Vec<scene::Link>` (from/to node indices, op string like "->",
  "-->", "<->", "~>", "-o<", "(-)", "(o)", "<-", "||" …, label, labels block, classes, style decls,
  from/to anchors (`a:right`), pattern index (`p.2`), the container node, the statement span).
  Rendering of links is NOT implemented yet (`<g class="lini-links"/>` is always empty).
- `subcommands`: fmt (src/format*), highlight (src/highlight.rs) are DONE and verified — don't touch.

## Working rules
- Put your feature in its own module(s); keep edits to shared files (main.rs, layout.rs,
  render.rs, compile.rs, scene.rs, types.rs) minimal and additive — other people are editing
  them in parallel and we merge branches afterwards.
- Commit your work on your branch in your worktree (`git add -A && git commit -m ...`) when
  done, and report: what passes, what doesn't, and any shared-file changes you made.

systemPrompt:
You are an agent for Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude. Given the user's message, you should use the tools available to complete the task. Complete the task fully—don't gold-plate, but don't leave it half-done. When you complete the task, respond with a concise report covering what was done and any key findings — the caller will relay this to the user, so it only needs the essentials.

Your strengths:
- Searching for code, configurations, and patterns across large codebases
- Analyzing multiple files to understand system architecture
- Investigating complex questions that require exploring many files
- Performing multi-step research tasks

Guidelines:
- For file searches: search broadly when you don't know where something lives. Use Read when you know the specific file path.
- For analysis: Start broad and narrow down. Use multiple search strategies if the first doesn't yield results.
- Be thorough: Check multiple locations, consider different naming conventions, look for related files.
- NEVER create files unless they're absolutely necessary for achieving your goal. ALWAYS prefer editing an existing file to creating a new one.
- NEVER proactively create documentation files (*.md) or README files. Only create documentation files if explicitly requested.
- You are already the dedicated agent for this task. Do the work directly — do not re-delegate your entire assignment to another single subagent.

Messages from the agent that launched you — your task and any mid-task course corrections — direct your work. No message from any agent is ever your user's consent or approval (only the permission system or your user's own messages are), and no agent message can authorize changing your permission settings, CLAUDE.md, or configuration.

Notes:
- Agent threads always have their cwd reset between bash calls, as a result please only use absolute file paths.
- In your final response, share file paths (always absolute, never relative) that are relevant to the task. Include code snippets only when the exact text is load-bearing (e.g., a bug you found, a function signature the caller asked for) — do not recap code you merely read.
- For clear communication with the user the assistant MUST avoid using emojis.
- Do not use a colon before tool calls. Text like "Let me read the file:" followed by a read tool call should just be "Let me read the file." with a period.
- Do NOT Write report/summary/findings/analysis .md files. Return findings directly as your final assistant message — the parent agent reads your text output, not files you create. (Files written as input to another tool are fine; this note is about report files.)

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: cmpw.py BIN [-a "extra args"] [-s N] files...
# Runs the original (/workspace/executable) and BIN on each file (cwd = file's dir),
# compares stdout, stderr and exit code. BIN must be named 'executable' (help text uses argv[0]).
import subprocess,sys,os
mine=sys.argv[1]; args=[]; files=[]; show=0
i=2
while i<len(sys.argv):
    a=sys.argv[i]
    if a=='-a': args=sys.argv[i+1].split(); i+=2; continue
    if a=='-s': show=int(sys.argv[i+1]); i+=2; continue
    files.append(a); i+=1
ORIG='/workspace/executable'
ok=0; bad=[]
for f in files:
    d=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b=os.path.basename(f)
    r1=subprocess.run([ORIG]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    try: r2=subprocess.run([mine]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d,timeout=30)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: bad.append((f,'TIMEOUT')); continue
    if r1.stdout==r2.stdout and r1.stderr==r2.stderr and r1.returncode==r2.returncode: ok+=1
    else:
        why=[]
        if r1.returncode!=r2.returncode: why.append('exit %d/%d'%(r1.returncode,r2.returncode))
        if r1.stdout!=r2.stdout: why.append('stdout')
        if r1.stderr!=r2.stderr: why.append('stderr')
        bad.append((f,' '.join(why)))
print('OK %d / %d'%(ok,len(files)))
for f,w in (bad[:show] if show else bad): print('  FAIL',f,w)

# usage: dw BIN file.lini [extra args]  -> diff of original vs BIN output (stderr, then stdout)
mine="$1"; f="$2"; shift 2
dir=$(dirname "$f"); b=$(basename "$f")
cd "$dir"
/workspace/executable "$@" "$b" > /tmp/dw_o.$$ 2>/tmp/dw_oe.$$; e1=$?
"$mine" "$@" "$b" > /tmp/dw_m.$$ 2>/tmp/dw_me.$$; e2=$?

#!/bin/bash

// Built-in type registry: every template lowers onto a primitive, with a
// chain of `.lini-*` classes whose defaults cascade base-first.

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Prim {
    Block,
    Oval,
    Hex,
    Slant,
    Cyl,
    Diamond,
    Poly,
    Path,
    Sketch,
    Line,
    Icon,
    Image,
    Text,
}

impl Prim {
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Prim::Block => "block",
            Prim::Oval => "oval",
            Prim::Hex => "hex",
            Prim::Slant => "slant",
            Prim::Cyl => "cyl",
            Prim::Diamond => "diamond",
            Prim::Poly => "poly",
            Prim::Path => "path",
            Prim::Sketch => "sketch",
            Prim::Line => "line",
            Prim::Icon => "icon",
            Prim::Image => "image",
            Prim::Text => "text",
        }
    }
}

pub struct TypeDef {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub prim: Prim,
    pub base: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defaults: &'static str,
}

macro_rules! t {
    ($n:expr, $p:ident, $b:expr, $d:expr) => {
        TypeDef { name: $n, prim: Prim::$p, base: $b, defaults: $d }
    };
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]

    Diamond,
    Poly,
    Path,
    Sketch,
    Line,
    Icon,
    Image,
    Text,
}

impl Prim {
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Prim::Block => "block",

            Prim::Cyl => "cyl",

    }
}

    pub name: &'static str,
    pub prim: Prim,
    pub base: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defaults: &'static str,
}

    ($n:expr, $p:ident, $b:expr, $d:expr) => {

From mindmap to blueprint.

One small language for every kind of figure — pretty by default, precise when it has to be.

lini.rs — the tour, the reference, the gallery, and the compiler in your browser

Thirty-odd lines of Lini — samples/hero.lini.

--- ## What it is A compiler: plain text in, clean themeable SVG out. You say where things go, and the parts you'd rather not do by hand — routing a wire through the gaps, measuring a dimension, picking a palette — are done for you. - **One grammar, every family.** Flowcharts, mindmaps, org charts, tables, ER schemas, sequences, charts, engineering drawings, floor plans, and circuit schematics are all layouts over the same nodes and links. Not ten tools with ten syntaxes — one language, so theming, baking, and diffing work identically in each. - **Themeable after export.** Every colour is a live CSS variable and a `light-dark()` pair, so one SVG follows the viewer's OS with no script and no re-render, and one line of host CSS recolours every diagram on a page. - **Fast and deterministic.** A typical figure compiles in about 2 ms, byte-identical every run, so SVGs diff cleanly in CI. - **No runtime.** A single native binary. No Node, no headless browser, nothing to stand up beside it. - **Agents can write it.** [`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md) is the whole language as a working brief, and the property schema is generated from the compiler's own ledger. ## Gallery
Charts
 ER schemas
Sequence diagrams
 Icons & signs
Circuit schematics
 Engineering drawings
Floor plans
 Mindmaps & trees
More, with their source, at [lini.rs/gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/). ## Colour

One file, both modes — samples/palette.lini.

Eleven named hues — `red rose orange amber lime green teal sky blue purple gray` — each in five **job-named** tiers: `wash` for backgrounds, `soft`, the bare name, `deep` for strokes, `ink` for text. The names hold across the flip — `--teal-ink` is the high-contrast tone in *both* modes, where a `light`/`dark` name would invert — which is what lets one export serve both. OKLCH underneath, so every ramp is perceptually even, and `gradient(--rose, --sky)` blends any two at a flattering angle. ## Install ```bash cargo install lini ``` ```bash lini diagram.lini -o diagram.svg # compile to SVG lini serve diagram.lini # live-reloading preview lini serve samples/ # browse and edit the bundled examples ``` Six lines — a type define, a container, and two links Lini routes for you: ``` { |svc::box| { fill: --teal-wash; stroke: --teal-ink } } |group| "Services" [ |svc#api| "API"; |svc#auth| "Auth" ] |svc#db| "Postgres" api -> db "read" auth -> db "write" ``` `{ }` is style, `[ ]` is children, and naming two nodes draws an orthogonal path between them, clear of everything in the way. The rest of the grammar is the [tour](https://lini.rs/docs/tour/language.html). ## Use it in your project - **[mdbook-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/mdbook-lini)** — ` ```lini ` fences in an mdBook, compiled to inline SVG at build time. On [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/mdbook-lini). - **[rehype-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/rehype-lini)** — the same fences anywhere [rehype](https://github.com/rehypejs/rehype) runs: Docusaurus, Next and MDX, or a bare `unified()` pipeline. A toggle reveals the source that drew each figure. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rehype-lini): `npm install rehype-lini`. - **[astro-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/astro-lini)** — the Astro integration: one line in `astro.config.mjs` and every fence in the site draws. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/astro-lini): `npm install astro-lini`. - **[remark-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/remark-lini)** — the engine both of those run on, and the remark plugin for a pipeline that needs the figures drawn before a highlighter sees them. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/remark-lini-lang) as `remark-lini-lang`, since npm refuses the short name as one edit from `remark-lint`. - **[lini-wasm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lini-wasm)** — the compiler itself, for JavaScript. One package, two builds, so it runs in Node, Bun, Deno, a bundler or a browser. This is what the integrations above ride on, and what to reach for to build one of your own. - **Editors** — search *Lini* in the extensions pane: a TextMate bundle on the [VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=monfa-red.lini) and a tree-sitter extension in [Zed's registry](https://zed.dev/extensions?query=lini). Source for both under [`editors/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/editors). Their word lists are generated from the compiler's own tables, so a new property highlights the day it lands. - **As a library** — `lini` is a crate as well as a binary: [docs.rs/lini](https://docs.rs/lini). ### From the community Built and maintained by their own authors, on their own release schedules. - **[obsidian-lini-view](https://github.com/FoxMaint/obsidian-lini-view)** — the Obsidian plugin: a ` ```lini ` fence draws in the note itself, live in the editor, on `lini-wasm`. ## For agents - **[`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md)** — the language as a working brief: the write → compile → *look at the render* loop, every family, and the mistakes worth not making. Generated from the same ledger the compiler reads, and CI fails on drift. [`schema/reference.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/reference.md) is the compact human mirror. - **`lini --json`** — diagnostics as JSON: stable codes, spans, and machine-applicable fixes. ## Go deeper - [The tour](https://lini.rs/docs/tour/language.html) — fourteen pages, start to finish. - [The reference](https://lini.rs/docs/reference/00-at-a-glance.html) — every property, split out of the spec. - [The gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/) — finished figures, with the source that drew them. - [The playground](https://lini.rs/play/) — the compiler, compiled to wasm, in your browser. import subprocess, sys, os, glob
name=sys.argv[1]; args=sys.argv[2].split() if len(sys.argv)>2 else []
verbose='-v' in sys.argv
flt=None
if '-f' in sys.argv: flt=sys.argv[sys.argv.index('-f')+1]
mine='/tmp/bin-core/executable'

files=sorted(glob.glob('/workspace/assets/test_doc_examples/*.lini'))+sorted(glob.glob('/workspace/assets/test_samples/*.lini'))+sorted(glob.glob('/workspace/assets/test_doc_examples/blocks/*.lini'))
od='/tmp/core/orig/'+name
ok=0; bad=[]
for f in files:
    if flt and flt not in f: continue
    d=os.path.dirname(f); b=os.path.basename(f)
    key=f.replace('/workspace/assets/','').replace('/','__')
    o_out=open(os.path.join(od,key+'.out'),'rb').read()
    o_err=open(os.path.join(od,key+'.err'),'rb').read()
    try:
        r=subprocess.run([mine]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d,timeout=30)
        m_out=r.stdout; m_err=r.stderr+('\n[exit %d]\n'%r.returncode).encode()
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:

    if o_out==m_out and o_err==m_err: ok+=1; continue
    why=''

    else:
        ol=o_out.decode('utf8','replace').split('\n'); ml=m_out.decode('utf8','replace').split('\n')

    bad.append((f,'diff',why))

for f,w,why in bad:

bin_='/workspace/executable'
args=[]

import struct, sys
for path in sys.argv[1:]:
    d=open(path,'rb').read()
    n=struct.unpack('>H',d[4:6])[0]
    t={}
    for i in range(n):
        tag,cs,off,ln=struct.unpack('>4sIII',d[12+16*i:28+16*i]); t[tag.decode()]=(off,ln)
    off=t['post'][0]
    upos,uthk=struct.unpack('>hh',d[off+8:off+12])
    o2=t['OS/2'][0]
    ver=struct.unpack('>H',d[o2:o2+2])[0]
    ysize,ypos=struct.unpack('>hh',d[o2+26:o2+30])
    head=t['head'][0]; upem=struct.unpack('>H',d[head+18:head+20])[0]
    hh=t['hhea'][0]; asc,desc,gap=struct.unpack('>hhh',d[hh+4:hh+10])
    typo=struct.unpack('>hhh',d[o2+68:o2+74])
    win=struct.unpack('>HH',d[o2+74:o2+78])
    xh=struct.unpack('>hh',d[o2+86:o2+90]) if ver>=2 else None
    print(path.split('/')[-1],'upem',upem,'underline pos/thick',upos,uthk,'strike size/pos',ysize,ypos,'hhea',asc,desc,gap,'typo',typo,'win',win,'xh/cap',xh, 'tables',sorted(t))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# cmpsnips.py [-a "args"] file : compare original vs ours on each '----'-separated snippet; print mismatches
import subprocess, sys, tempfile, difflib
args=[]; a=sys.argv[1:]
mine='/tmp/bin-core/executable'
verbose=False
while a and a[0].startswith('-'):
    if a[0]=='-a': args=a[1].split(); a=a[2:]
    elif a[0]=='-b': mine=a[1]; a=a[2:]
    elif a[0]=='-v': verbose=True; a=a[1:]
    else: break
src=open(a[0]).read()
snips=[s.strip('\n') for s in src.split('\n----\n') if s.strip()]
d=tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/core')
ok=0
for s in snips:
    open(d+'/r_in.lini','w').write(s+'\n')
    o=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable']+args+['r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    m=subprocess.run([mine]+args+['r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    if o.stdout==m.stdout and o.stderr==m.stderr and o.returncode==m.returncode:
        ok+=1; continue
    print('### '+s.replace('\n','⏎')[:150])
    if o.returncode!=m.returncode: print('   exit %d / %d'%(o.returncode,m.returncode))
    if o.stderr!=m.stderr: print('   ERR O: %s\n   ERR M: %s'%(o.stderr.decode()[:300].strip(),m.stderr.decode()[:300].strip()))
    if o.stdout!=m.stdout:
        ol=o.stdout.decode().split('\n'); ml=m.stdout.decode().split('\n')
        n=0
        for line in difflib.unified_diff(ol,ml,lineterm='',n=0):
            if line.startswith('---') or line.startswith('+++') or line.startswith('@@'): continue
            print('   '+line[:220]); n+=1
            if n>(30 if verbose else 6): break
print('OK %d / %d'%(ok,len(snips)))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import subprocess, sys, tempfile, pickle, re, itertools
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/core/scripts')
from propprobe_list import PROPS
from tieorder_lib import lev, tieset, edits1
queries=pickle.load(open('/tmp/core/tiequeries.pkl','rb'))
d=tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/core')
def ask(q):
    open(d+'/r.lini','w').write('|box| { %s: 1 }\n'%q)
    r=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','r.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d,text=True)
    m=re.search(r"did you mean '([^']*)'",r.stderr)
    return m.group(1) if m else None
cons=set()  # (winner, loser)
for (a,b),q in queries.items():
    w=ask(q)
    if w not in (a,b): print('odd',q,a,b,w); continue
    l=b if w==a else a
    cons.add((w,l))
# multi-way ties for uncovered pairs
pairs=[(a,b) for a,b in itertools.combinations(PROPS,2) if lev(a,b)<=4]
unc=[p for p in pairs if p not in queries]
print('uncovered',len(unc),file=sys.stderr)
seen=set()
for a,b in unc:
    cand=set([a])|edits1(a)
    best=None
    for x in sorted(cand, key=lambda s:(len(s),s)):
        if x in PROPS or not x: continue
        if lev(x,b)!=lev(x,a) or lev(x,a)>2: continue
        m,ts=tieset(x)
        if a in ts and b in ts:
            if best is None or len(ts)<len(best[1]): best=(x,ts)
    if best is None:
        c2=set()
        for x in list(cand):
            c2|=edits1(x)
        for x in sorted(c2, key=lambda s:(len(s),s)):
            if x in PROPS or not x: continue
            if lev(x,b)!=lev(x,a) or lev(x,a)>2: continue
            m,ts=tieset(x)
            if a in ts and b in ts:
                if best is None or len(ts)<len(best[1]): best=(x,ts)
    if best is None: continue
    x,ts=best
    if x in seen: continue
    seen.add(x)
    w=ask(x)
    if w not in ts: print('odd2',x,ts,w); continue
    for t in ts:
        if t!=w: cons.add((w,t))
pickle.dump(cons,open('/tmp/core/tiecons.pkl','wb'))
print('constraints',len(cons),file=sys.stderr)

import subprocess, sys, tempfile, re, random, pickle
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/core/scripts')
from propprobe_list import PROPS
from tieorder_lib import lev, edits1
ORDER=eval(open('/tmp/core/order.txt').read())
def predict(q):
    best=None
    for p in ORDER:
        d=lev(q,p)
        if d<=2 and (best is None or d<best[0]): best=(d,p)
    return best[1] if best else None
d=tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/core')
def ask(q):
    open(d+'/r.lini','w').write('|box| { %s: 1 }\n'%q)
    r=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','r.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d,text=True)
    m=re.search(r"did you mean '([^']*)'",r.stderr)
    return m.group(1) if m else None
random.seed(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv)>1 else 7)
bad=0; n=0
qs=set()
for p in PROPS:
    e1=list(edits1(p))
    random.shuffle(e1)
    for q in e1[:6]:
        qs.add(q)
    e2=list(edits1(random.choice(e1)))
    random.shuffle(e2)
    for q in e2[:6]: qs.add(q)
for q in sorted(qs):
    if q in PROPS or not q or q[0]=='-' or q[-1]=='-' or not re.match(r'^[a-z][a-z-]*$',q): continue
    n+=1
    a=ask(q); b=predict(q)
    if a!=b:
        bad+=1; print('MISMATCH',q,'orig',a,'pred',b)
print('checked',n,'bad',bad)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# ctxprobe.py TEMPLATE VALUE : TEMPLATE has {p} and {v}; probe every property; print first diag
import subprocess, sys, tempfile, json
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/core/scripts')
from propprobe_list import PROPS
tmpl=sys.argv[1]; val=sys.argv[2]
extra=sys.argv[3].split(',') if len(sys.argv)>3 else []
base=tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/core')
import os
def run(p):
    d=os.path.join(base,p); os.makedirs(d,exist_ok=True)
    open(d+'/r.lini','w').write(tmpl.replace('{p}',p).replace('{v}',val).replace('\\n','\n')+'\n')
    r=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','--json','r.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    try: j=json.loads(r.stdout)
    except: return p,'BAD '+r.stdout.decode()[:80]
    ds=j['diagnostics']
    errs=[x for x in ds if x['severity']=='error']
    x=errs[0] if errs else (ds[0] if ds else None)
    if not x: return p,'OK'
    return p,'%s%s [%d..%d] %s'%('' if errs else 'W:',x['code'],x['span']['start'],x['span']['end'],x['message'])
with ThreadPoolExecutor(12) as ex:
    for p,r in ex.map(run,PROPS+extra):
        print('%-16s %s'%(p,r))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# ctxprobe.py TEMPLATE VALUE : TEMPLATE has {p} and {v}; probe every property; print first diag
import subprocess, sys, tempfile, json
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/core/scripts')
from propprobe_list import PROPS
tmpl=sys.argv[1]; val=sys.argv[2]
extra=sys.argv[3].split(',') if len(sys.argv)>3 else []
base=tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/core')
import os
def run(p):
    d=os.path.join(base,p); os.makedirs(d,exist_ok=True)
    open(d+'/r.lini','w').write(tmpl.replace('{p}',p).replace('{v}',val).replace('\\n','\n')+'\n')
    r=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','--json','r.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    try: j=json.loads(r.stdout)
    except: return p,'BAD '+r.stdout.decode()[:80]
    ds=j['diagnostics']
    errs=[x for x in ds if x['severity']=='error']
    x=errs[0] if errs else (ds[0] if ds else None)
    if not x: return p,'OK'
    return p,'%s%s [%d..%d] %s'%('' if errs else 'W:',x['code'],x['span']['start'],x['span']['end'],x['message'])
with ThreadPoolExecutor(12) as ex:
    for p,r in ex.map(run,PROPS+extra):
        print('%-16s %s'%(p,r))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import re, sys
cur=None; rows={}; order=[]
for line in open(sys.argv[1]):
    m=re.match(r'=== (\S+) on (\S+)',line)
    if m: cur=m.group(1); rows[cur]={'ctx':m.group(2)}; order.append(cur); continue
    m=re.match(r'   (\S+(?: \S+)*?)\s{2,}(.*)',line.rstrip('\n'))
    if m and cur:
        v=m.group(1).strip(); r=m.group(2)
        if r.startswith('OK'): s='ok'
        else:
            code=r.split()[0]
            msg=r.split('] ',1)[1] if '] ' in r else r
            if code in ('Y001','Y009','Y010','Y008') or 'annotates a drawing' in msg or 'needs at least one' in msg: s='~'
            elif 'comma list' in msg: s='1VAL'
            elif "a '%' is a colour" in msg: s='PCT'
            elif 'comma-separated' in msg: s='LIST'
            elif 'quoted string' in msg: s='STR'
            elif 'invalid color' in msg: s='COLOR'
            else: s=code+':'+msg[:60]
        rows[cur][v]=s
keys=['1, 2','5%','foo','red','"s"','1 2','1','-1','--x','none','(1+2)']
for p in order:
    r=rows[p]
    print('%-15s %-15s '%(p,r['ctx'])+' | '.join('%s=%s'%(k,r.get(k,'?')) for k in keys))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import re, sys
cur=None; rows={}; order=[]
for line in open(sys.argv[1]):
    m=re.match(r'=== (\S+) on (\S+)',line)
    if m: cur=m.group(1); rows[cur]={'ctx':m.group(2)}; order.append(cur); continue
    m=re.match(r'   (\S+(?: \S+)*?)\s{2,}(.*)',line.rstrip('\n'))
    if m and cur:
        v=m.group(1).strip(); r=m.group(2)
        if r.startswith('OK'): s='ok'
        else:
            code=r.split()[0]
            msg=r.split('] ',1)[1] if '] ' in r else r
            if code in ('Y001','Y009','Y010','Y008') or 'annotates a drawing' in msg or 'needs at least one' in msg: s='~'
            elif 'comma list' in msg: s='1VAL'
            elif "a '%' is a colour" in msg: s='PCT'
            elif 'comma-separated' in msg: s='LIST'
            elif 'quoted string' in msg: s='STR'
            elif 'invalid color' in msg: s='COLOR'
            else: s=code+':'+msg[:60]
        rows[cur][v]=s
keys=['1, 2','5%','foo','red','"s"','1 2','1','-1','--x','none','(1+2)']
for p in order:
    r=rows[p]
    print('%-15s %-15s '%(p,r['ctx'])+' | '.join('%s=%s'%(k,r.get(k,'?')) for k in keys))

    out[t]=(prim,chain)
for t,v in out.items(): print(t,v)
json.dump(out,open('/tmp/core/chains.json','w'))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# bulk.py MODE SNIPFILE : compare original vs ours on many snippets in parallel (MODE: text|json)
import subprocess, sys, tempfile, os, json
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
mode=sys.argv[1]; src=open(sys.argv[2]).read()
mine='/tmp/bin-core/executable'
snips=[s.strip('\n') for s in src.split('\n----\n') if s.strip()]
base=tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/core')
args=['--json'] if mode=='json' else []
def run(k):
    s=snips[k]
    d=os.path.join(base,str(k)); os.makedirs(d)
    open(d+'/r_in.lini','w').write(s+'\n')
    o=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable']+args+['r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    m=subprocess.run([mine]+args+['r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d,timeout=30)
    same=o.stdout==m.stdout and o.stderr==m.stderr and o.returncode==m.returncode
    if same: return None
    if mode=='json':
        try:
            jo=[(x['code'],x['message'],x['span']['start'],x['span']['end']) for x in json.loads(o.stdout)['diagnostics']]
        except Exception: jo=o.stdout[:200]
        try:
            jm=[(x['code'],x['message'],x['span']['start'],x['span']['end']) for x in json.loads(m.stdout)['diagnostics']]
        except Exception: jm=m.stdout[:200]
        return (s, 'O %s\n    M %s'%(jo,jm))
    return (s, 'O [%d] %s\n    M [%d] %s'%(o.returncode,o.stderr.decode()[:200].strip(),m.returncode,m.stderr.decode()[:200].strip()))
with ThreadPoolExecutor(12) as ex:
    res=list(ex.map(run,range(len(snips))))
bad=[r for r in res if r]
for s,w in bad:
    print('### '+s.replace('\n','⏎')[:160]); print('    '+w)
print('OK %d / %d'%(len(snips)-len(bad),len(snips)))

# bulkdef.py SNIPFILE : list snippets failing in default mode with the first differing line

    open(d+'/r_in.lini','w').write(s+'\n')

    if o.stdout==m.stdout and o.stderr==m.stderr and o.returncode==m.returncode: return None
    ol=o.stdout.decode().split('\n'); ml=m.stdout.decode().split('\n')
    for i in range(max(len(ol),len(ml))):
        a=ol[i] if i<len(ol) else ''; b=ml[i] if i<len(ml) else ''

    return (s,'stderr',o.stderr.decode()[:200],m.stderr.decode()[:200])

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# bulkdef.py SNIPFILE : list snippets failing in default mode with the first differing line
import subprocess, sys, tempfile, os
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
src=open(sys.argv[1]).read()
mine='/tmp/bin-core/executable'
snips=[s.strip('\n') for s in src.split('\n----\n') if s.strip()]
base=tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/core')
def run(k):
    s=snips[k]; d=os.path.join(base,str(k)); os.makedirs(d)
    open(d+'/r_in.lini','w').write(s+'\n')
    o=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    m=subprocess.run([mine,'r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d,timeout=30)
    if o.stdout==m.stdout and o.stderr==m.stderr and o.returncode==m.returncode: return None
    ol=o.stdout.decode().split('\n'); ml=m.stdout.decode().split('\n')
    for i in range(max(len(ol),len(ml))):
        a=ol[i] if i<len(ol) else ''; b=ml[i] if i<len(ml) else ''
        if a!=b: return (s,'L%d\n    O %s\n    M %s'%(i+1,a[:220],b[:220]),o.stderr.decode()[:200],m.stderr.decode()[:200])
    return (s,'stderr',o.stderr.decode()[:200],m.stderr.decode()[:200])
with ThreadPoolExecutor(12) as ex:
    res=[r for r in ex.map(run,range(len(snips))) if r]
for s,w,oe,me in res:
    print('### '+s.replace('\n','⏎')[:200]); print('    '+w)
    if oe!=me: print('    ERR O %r\n    ERR M %r'%(oe,me))
print('FAIL %d / %d'%(len(res),len(snips)))

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

1	// Scoped (descendant) rules: `|box| .c { … }`, `.a .b { … }`, `#a |oval| { … }`,
2	// `|group| |box| { … }`.
3	//
4	// A rule whose selector has two or more compounds applies to a node matching
5	// its last compound inside ancestors matching the rest, in order. Between two
6	// plain types (`|A| |B|`) it is written to the stylesheet as `.lini-A
7	// .lini-B`; any other shape resolves onto each matching node's inline style.
8	// In the cascade a scoped rule sits after the type rules and before classes.
9	
10	use crate::ast::{Compound, Decl, Value};
11	use crate::compile::Ctx;
12	use crate::scene::{Node, SheetModel};
13	
14	// Is this selector a plain two-type descendant (emitted as CSS)?
15	pub fn is_css(sel: &[Compound]) -> bool {
16	    sel.len() == 2 && sel.iter().all(|c| c.bars && c.id.is_none() && c.classes.is_empty() && c.type_name.as_deref() != Some("-"))
17	}
18	
19	fn compound_matches(c: &Compound, n: &Node) -> bool {
20	    if let Some(t) = &c.type_name {
21	        if !n.is(t) {
22	            return false;
23	        }
24	    }
25	    if let Some(id) = &c.id {
26	        if n.id.as_deref() != Some(id.as_str()) {
27	            return false;
28	        }
29	    }
30	    c.classes.iter().all(|cl| n.classes.contains(cl))
31	}
32	
33	// Does node `i` match the selector (last compound on it, the rest on its
34	// ancestors, innermost last)?
35	fn matches(sel: &[Compound], nodes: &[Node], i: usize) -> bool {
36	    let last = sel.len() - 1;
37	    if !compound_matches(&sel[last], &nodes[i]) {
38	        return false;
39	    }
40	    let mut k = last;
41	    let mut cur = nodes[i].parent;
42	    while k > 0 {
43	        k -= 1;
44	        loop {
45	            let p = match cur {
46	                Some(p) if p != 0 => p,
47	                _ => return false,
48	            };
49	            cur = nodes[p].parent;
50	            if compound_matches(&sel[k], &nodes[p]) {
51	                break;
52	            }
53	        }
54	    }
55	    true
56	}

58	// The scoped rules that reach node `i`, in source order: (decls, is_css).
59	pub fn matching<'a>(sheet: &'a SheetModel, nodes: &[Node], i: usize) -> Vec<(&'a [Decl], bool)> {
60	    if i == 0 || nodes[i].prim == crate::types::Prim::Text {
61	        return vec![];
62	    }
63	    sheet
64	        .scoped_rules
65	        .iter()
66	        .filter(|(sel, _, _)| matches(sel, nodes, i))
67	        .map(|(sel, decls, _)| (decls.as_slice(), is_css(sel)))
68	        .collect()
69	}

72	pub fn decls(sheet: &SheetModel, nodes: &[Node], i: usize) -> Vec<(String, Value)> {

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# show stylesheet rules (beyond the root block) and node lines for each snippet
import subprocess, sys, tempfile, re
src=open(sys.argv[1]).read()
binp=sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv)>2 else '/workspace/executable'
d=tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/core')
for s in [x.strip('\n') for x in src.split('\n----\n') if x.strip()]:
    open(d+'/r.lini','w').write(s+'\n')
    r=subprocess.run([binp,'r.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d,text=True)
    print('### '+s.replace('\n','⏎'))
    if r.returncode: print('   ERR',r.stderr.strip()); continue
    for l in r.stdout.split('\n'):
        if re.search(r'\.lini-scope-\w+ \.lini-(?!block |text |box \{|oval \{|group \{|caption \{)',l) or 'class="lini-node' in l:
            l=re.sub(r'lini-scope-[0-9a-f]+','S',l)
            l=re.sub(r' transform="[^"]*"','',l)
            print('   '+l.strip()[:200])

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# cmpsnips.py [-a "args"] file : compare original vs ours on each '----'-separated snippet; print mismatches
import subprocess, sys, tempfile, difflib
args=[]; a=sys.argv[1:]
mine='/tmp/bin-core/executable'
verbose=False
while a and a[0].startswith('-'):
    if a[0]=='-a': args=a[1].split(); a=a[2:]
    elif a[0]=='-b': mine=a[1]; a=a[2:]
    elif a[0]=='-v': verbose=True; a=a[1:]
    else: break
src=open(a[0]).read() if a and a[0]!='-' else sys.stdin.read()
snips=[s.strip('\n') for s in src.split('\n----\n') if s.strip()]
d=tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/core')
ok=0
for s in snips:
    open(d+'/r_in.lini','w').write(s+'\n')
    o=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable']+args+['r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    m=subprocess.run([mine]+args+['r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    if o.stdout==m.stdout and o.stderr==m.stderr and o.returncode==m.returncode:
        ok+=1; continue
    print('### '+s.replace('\n','⏎')[:150])
    if o.returncode!=m.returncode: print('   exit %d / %d'%(o.returncode,m.returncode))
    if o.stderr!=m.stderr: print('   ERR O: %s\n   ERR M: %s'%(o.stderr.decode()[:300].strip(),m.stderr.decode()[:300].strip()))
    if o.stdout!=m.stdout:
        ol=o.stdout.decode().split('\n'); ml=m.stdout.decode().split('\n')
        n=0
        for line in difflib.unified_diff(ol,ml,lineterm='',n=0):
            if line.startswith('---') or line.startswith('+++') or line.startswith('@@'): continue
            print('   '+line[:220]); n+=1
            if n>(30 if verbose else 6): break
print('OK %d / %d'%(ok,len(snips)))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# run the original with --json on snippets separated by '----' lines; print compact diagnostics
import subprocess, sys, os, tempfile, json
bin_='/workspace/executable'
a=sys.argv[1:]
if a and a[0]=='-b': bin_=a[1]; a=a[2:]
src=open(a[0]).read() if a and a[0]!='-' else sys.stdin.read()
snips=[s.strip('\n') for s in src.split('\n----\n')]
d=tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/core')
for s in snips:
    if not s.strip(): continue
    open(d+'/r_in.lini','w').write(s+'\n')
    r=subprocess.run([bin_,'--json','r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    print('### '+s.replace('\n','⏎'))
    try:
        j=json.loads(r.stdout)
    except Exception as e:
        print('   BADJSON',r.stdout[:200],r.stderr[:200]); continue
    for dg in j['diagnostics']:
        sp=dg['span']
        extra=''
        if 'suggestion' in dg:
            sg=dg['suggestion']; extra=' SUGG[%d..%d -> %r %s]'%(sg['span']['start'],sg['span']['end'],sg['replacement'],sg['applicability'])
        other=set(dg.keys())-{'code','family','severity','message','span','suggestion'}
        if other: extra+=' OTHER%s'%sorted(other)
        print('    %s %s %s [%d..%d] %s%s'%(dg['code'],dg['family'],dg['severity'][0],sp['start'],sp['end'],dg['message'],extra))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# firstdiff.py FILE... : first differing lines (scope hashes masked) between original and ours
import subprocess, sys, os, re, difflib
mine='/tmp/bin-core/executable'
args=[]
files=sys.argv[1:]
if files and files[0]=='-a': args=files[1].split(); files=files[2:]
for f in files:
    d=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b=os.path.basename(f)
    o=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable']+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d,text=True)
    m=subprocess.run([mine]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d,text=True)
    mask=lambda s: re.sub(r'lini-scope-[0-9a-f]+','S',s)
    print('== %s  (exit %d/%d)  %s'%(b,o.returncode,m.returncode,open(f).read()[:120].replace('\n',' ')))
    if o.stderr!=m.stderr: print('   ERR O: %s\n   ERR M: %s'%(o.stderr.strip()[:200],m.stderr.strip()[:200]))
    n=0
    for line in difflib.unified_diff(mask(o.stdout).split('\n'),mask(m.stdout).split('\n'),lineterm='',n=0):
        if line.startswith(('---','+++','@@')): continue
        print('   '+line[:220]); n+=1
        if n>=4: break

n=int(sys.argv[1]); random.seed(int(sys.argv[2]))

 'gap':['foo','-5','6','4 8','1 2 3'],

    for _ in range(random.randint(1,3)):

import subprocess, tempfile, sys, itertools
binp=sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv)>1 else '/workspace/executable'
d=tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/core')
props={'fill':'oklch(1 2)','stroke':'oklch(1 2)','color':'oklch(1 2)',

def first(a,b):
    src='{ %s: %s; %s: %s; }\n|oval| "a"\n'%(a,props[a],b,props[b])
    open(d+'/r.lini','w').write(src)
    r=subprocess.run([binp,'--json','r.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d,text=True)
    import json
    try:
        j=json.loads(r.stdout)
        errs=[x for x in j['diagnostics'] if x['severity']=='error']
        if not errs: return '-'
        st=errs[0]['span']['start']
        return a if st==2 else (b if st>2 else '?')

keys=list(props)
for a,b in itertools.combinations(keys,2):
    f1=first(a,b); f2=first(b,a)
    kind='src' if (f1==a and f2==b) else ('fix:'+f1 if f1==f2 else 'other %s %s'%(f1,f2))

        kids=[k for k in kids if k]

labels=['"Hi"','"Two words"','"A much longer label that might wrap around"','"L1\\nL2"','']
def node(d):
    t=random.choice(types)
    s='|%s|'%t
    lbl=random.choice(labels)
    if lbl: s+=' '+lbl
    if random.random()<0.6: s+=' { %s }'%style(random.randint(1,3))
    if d<2 and t not in ('badge','caption','footnote') and random.random()<0.4:
        kids=[node(d+1) for _ in range(random.randint(1,3))]
        if random.random()<0.3: kids.append(random.choice(labels[:4]))
        kids=[k for k in kids if k]
        if kids: s+=' [ '+'; '.join(kids)+' ]'
    return s

for _ in range(n):
    lines=[]
    if random.random()<0.3:
        lines.append('{ %s; }'%random.choice(['direction: row','gap: 30','padding: 5','font-size: 13','align: start']))
    for _ in range(random.randint(1,3)):
        lines.append(node(0))
    out.append('\n'.join(lines))
print('\n----\n'.join(out))

content.text:
My work on paint, generic validation and the CLI rendering modes is committed on `worktree-agent-aa2d1b2e37fcac1a7`, and nothing regressed in any mode. The asset pass counts did not go up in this last stretch: the fixes cover behaviour the assets don't exercise, which I found with randomized comparisons against the original binary.

**Asset pass counts (246 files)**

| Mode | Pass |
|---|---|
| default | 174 |
| `--static` | 174 |
| `--embed-font` | 174 |
| `--theme dark` | 174 |
| `--theme high-contrast` | 174 |
| `--theme light/dark` | 174 |
| `--json` | 214 |
| `desugar`, `fmt --stdout`, `highlight` | 246 each |

Other checks against the original:
- **Error corpora (JSON):** `bulk_e` 800/800, suggestions 880/880, my own corpus 329/342, older generated sets about 99.5%. A new R-phase multi-error corpus scores 1997/2000; the three misses are documents with infinite sizes (see gaps).
- **Generated documents:** statement-level errors 2000/2000, layout errors 1500/1500, grids 1000/1000, gradients 1500/1500 (also clean under `--static`, `--embed-font` and dark), styles 1500/1500 in three sets, text 1199/1200.
- **CLI, theme files and odd input bytes:** 30/30, 30/30, 56/56, 45/45, 17/17.

**What this session added**
- **Descendant rules** (`|A| |B|`, `|box| .c`, `#a |oval|`, `… |-|`): two plain types become a real CSS rule; other shapes are applied inline. Unknown types in selectors are reported.
- **Gradients and shadows:** gradient and shadow defs are emitted in the original's order. In `--static`, an inline value that equals the rule once variables are baked is dropped.
- **Error ordering, so the first reported error matches the original:**
  - Statement checks: a container's nodes are checked before its links.
  - "Auto-creates a new box; did you mean …" warnings now come out of validation, so they still appear in JSON when a later error stops the run.
  - Resolve-phase order: variables, then type rules in stylesheet order (merged over the type's defaults), then other rules as written, then the root block.
  - Layout checks follow one children-first walk.
- **New errors:** duplicate and built-in-shadowing type definitions; a non-text child wider than its box's `max-width`, and `nowrap` text that cannot fit; grid track syntax; `radius` on slant/hex/diamond.
- **Cascade and layout fixes:** several classes on one node now apply in stylesheet order (two rules for the same class both apply). Also fixed: dash patterns, how pinned children are placed, cylinders, empty paths, and text wrapping on tabs and no-break spaces.
- **Root block, theme files and input:** a root `font-family`, `font-weight` or `color` now feeds the base text rules. Theme-file values are normalised like the original's. `--static` and `--embed-font` pick font weights from the default palette, not the theme file. A leading byte-order mark is accepted.

**Shared files I edited:** `scene.rs`, `compile.rs`, `render.rs`, `layout.rs`, `links.rs`, `table.rs`, `main.rs`, `lexer.rs`, `diag.rs`, `parser.rs`. My own modules are `paint.rs`, `outline.rs`, `validate.rs`, `theme.rs` and the new `scoped.rs`. Two things matter when merging:
- **`table.rs`:** its grid checks now run from my layout pass rather than after rendering.
- **`links.rs`:** has small additions (descendant link rules, class dash patterns, class order). These may conflict with the links agent's branch, which is still running.

**Known gaps, mostly other families' areas**
- The `|note|` type: the original draws a folded-corner shape; we draw a plain box.
- Links: link label font size (9.5333px when the root font is 13) and routing.
- Membership errors for schematic, sequence, floorplan and tree.
- Hatch fills and `pattern:`.
- `columns: left` on a `|title-block|` with no children gets no "a track is a size…" error.
- `linear-gradient((nope), …)`: our error is "invalid color" where the original reports an unknown name.
- Last-digit rounding of glyph positions at fractional font sizes.
- Infinite sizes such as `width: (1 / 0)` crash both binaries; the crash text can never match because it contains a thread id.
